answer.rationale: P99 latency is 5x target on the write path during peak settlement traffic. A rollback is impossible due to the non-revertible security patch. Adding capacity takes time we don't have; circuit breakers don't address root latency. Memory b5 shows that routing report queries to read replicas reduced primary load and allowed transactional latency to recover the same day. This mirrors our situation: heavy write load plus likely dashboard/reporting queries on the primary. Starting with a small guarded test of read replica routing for non-transactional queries preserves the security patch, protects customer writes, and can be monitored closely during peak settlement. If successful, we can broaden. If not, we haven't consumed our single intervention window beyond safe experimentation.
